messages:
nisha: follow-up on continuous-batching tradeoffs. proposal: extract ordering into a small OrderingPolicy plugin so we can try score-based and affinity-preserving strategies without touching core enqueue logic. short notes + canary plan.

aj: sounds promising. main verification vectors? tail latency, kvcache skew, and determinism for per-GPU queues?

nisha: exactly. must keep per-gpu enqueue deterministic; policy can only reorder within a bounded window. start with shadow mode then percent rollout.

oliver: bounded window is key. reordering increases memory and worst-case latency if unbounded. propose a max-reorder-depth and a cost model: if simulated cache_delta > epsilon prefer affinity.

sam: implementation sketch: OrderingPolicy.apply(req) -> score. default FIFO returns monotonic score. only if score_delta > threshold we consider moving across the window. add a reorder_id tag for telemetry.

maria: telemetry: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, reorder_rate, kvcache_hit_rate_by_policy, batches_changed, token_throughput. add policy_id label. set alarm if p999 > baseline * 1.15.

chloe: rollout: 1) shadow mode for 100% traffic for 24h, collect simulated cache delta and batch shapes. 2) enable ordered_percent=10 in us-west for 48h. 3) expand to 50% with region rotation. rollback: instant revert to FIFO on error-budget breach.

runtime-bot: ci: order-plugin branch built, unit tests + arrival-trace sim passed :white_check_mark:

nisha: next steps: spike PR (shadow), small sim run on last week's arrival trace, dashboard (sam/aj), sync tomorrow 30m to pick thresholds. thanks all.
